claims.claim: Spotify requires at least 3 chapters per episode and the first chapter must start at 00:00.
claims.raw_snippet: Your first chapter should start at 00:00 or 00:00:00

claims.claim: Spotify accepts (MM:SS), MM:SS, (HH:MM:SS) and HH:MM:SS chapter timestamp formats written in the episode description.
claims.raw_snippet: (MM:SS); MM:SS; (HH:MM:SS); and HH:MM:SS are all accepted timestamp formats

claims.claim: Spotify requires a minimum of 3 chapters.
The Podcasting 2.0 JSON Chapters format requires a version string and an array of chapters; startTime is expressed in seconds.
claims.raw_snippet: - `startTime` (required - float) The starting time of the chapter, expressed in seconds with float precision for fractions of a second.

claims.claim: The JSON Chapters example in the Podcasting 2.0 spec uses version 1.2.0.
The <podcast:chapters> RSS tag references the chapters file with a required url attribute and the application/json+chapters mime type.
claims.raw_snippet: Mime type of file - JSON prefered, ‘application/json+chapters’.

claims.claim: Apple Podcasts ingests <podcast:transcript> (VTT/SRT) but its auto-generated transcript languages exclude Hebrew; hosted transcripts in any language can still be referenced.
FFmpeg's subtitles filter passes SRTs through libass and supports force_style; libass needs FriBidi + HarfBuzz to render Hebrew RTL correctly.
libass requires FriBidi (bidi resolution) and HarfBuzz (shaping) to render Hebrew/Arabic; without them text renders mirrored.
Heebo is a Hebrew-capable Google Font usable for subtitle rendering.
The macOS Homebrew core formula ffmpeg-full bundles libass and HarfBuzz (FriBidi transitively via libass); the default ffmpeg formula does not, and Homebrew no longer supports --with-* options.

The clip shareability scoring weights are this skill's own heuristic, not external facts: quotable density 40%, emotional peaks 25%, standalone comprehensibility 20%, topic hook 15% (sum 100%). They are tunable in scripts/score_segments.py.
example.com is an IANA-reserved second-level domain name (RFC 2606) intended only for use as an example.
The example.com / cdn.example.com URLs in the chapter and RSS examples are illustrative placeholders on an RFC 2606 reserved domain, not live endpoints.
